en: Clients, engagements, fees, risk and capacity for accounting practices
Clients, engagements, fees per hour, onboarding, risk and capacity in one file
Fees against hours for every client
yearly fees, staff cost of the hours worked, margin and fee per hour for each client, with the ones below your minimum margin flagged
each service a client buys, the discount to list price, the yearly value and a renewal status before the date passes
Fee schedule with the real discount you give
list price, cost to deliver, margin and the average discount actually charged, service by service
identity, engagement letter, bank access, previous adviser letter and tax authority form, with the next missing check and days open
Fee increase planner with letter dates
new fee, extra income per year, the day the letter must go out for your notice period and what is still to send
chance and weighted value by stage, days since the last touch, quote expiry dates and your real win rate
leads and clients from each bank, lawyer or network, the fees they brought, the reward earned and what is still owed
every request with its due date, received date and days late, so you see which clients hold up the work
Client risk score with review dates
six factors added into a level, compared with the level on the client file, with the next review date
payment habits, papers on time, contact, complaints, margin and satisfaction rolled into one score with a healthy, watch or at-risk band
next year-end, days to go, filing deadline and where the accounts stand: waiting, records in, draft sent or filed
net hours, hours worked, utilisation and free hours for every person and month, with overloaded and spare people flagged
why each client left, the yearly fees lost and the day to send the win-back note

One row per client business: who looks after it, fees, risk and year-end. Yearly fees, hours, margin, fee per hour, last contact and health score fill in by themselves.
One row per client and service: start, agreed fee and renewal date. Discount to list, yearly value, hours, fee per hour and renewal status fill in by themselves.
Your price list by service. Price per hour, cost to deliver, margin, live engagements, yearly fees and the average discount you really give fill in by themselves.
Everyone you deal with at each client: role, preferred way to reach them and who signs or decides. The business name and client status fill in by themselves.
The five checks before work starts: identity, engagement letter, bank access, previous adviser letter and tax authority form. Missing checks, days open and readiness fill in by themselves.
Each planned fee increase: the new fee, the extra per year, the date to send the letter and the answer. Letters you still have to send are flagged.
Every enquiry from first contact to won or lost. Days waiting, chance of winning, yearly value, weighted value and the cold flag fill in by themselves.
Every quote sent: fee, set-up fee, expiry and outcome. Days left, first-year value, days to decide and the follow-up status fill in by themselves.
Banks, law firms, networks and clients who send you work. Leads, clients won, yearly fees, reward earned and reward owed fill in by themselves.
Every paper you ask a client for: due date and when it arrived. Status, days late and days to receive fill in by themselves, so slow clients stand out.
Score six risk factors from 1 to 3 for each client. Risk points, assessed level, a check against the client file and the next review date fill in by themselves.
A 0 to 100 score per client from payment habits, papers on time, contact, open complaints, margin and satisfaction. Clients below your limit are flagged as at risk.
Every meeting, call and visit with a client and what was promised afterwards. Hours spent and overdue follow-ups fill in by themselves; future dates show as booked.
Complaints, praise and suggestions with how fast you replied and closed them. Status, days to reply and whether you met your own reply rule fill in by themselves.
Each client's year-ends: last and next year-end, filing deadline and where the annual accounts stand. Deadline status and the days to the next year-end fill in by themselves.
Every client who left and why, with the fees lost and the day to send a win-back note. Fees lost per year, fees earned in total and the win-back status fill in by themselves.

Hello {contact}, welcome! {staff} will be your account manager. We will send a short list of the papers we need first. Reply here with any question.
Hello {contact}, it is time for your yearly review. Shall we book 30 minutes this month to look at the results of {name}, our fees and your plans?
Hello {contact}, thank you for {months} months with us. If you know a business that needs help with its books, we would be glad to meet them.
We have not spoken for a while
Hello {contact}, we have not spoken for {idle} days. Is everything fine with {name}? Reply with a good time for a short call.
Hello {contact}, please send us your {doc} by {due}. A photo or PDF is fine. Thank you!
Hello {contact}, a friendly reminder: we still need your {doc}, due on {due}. Please send it here as a photo or PDF.
Hello {contact}, your {doc} are now {days_late} days late and we cannot finish your work without them. Please send them today or tell us when they will come.
Hello {contact}, we received your {doc}. Thank you! We will start work now.
Hello {contact}, this confirms our {mtype} on {date} about {topic}. It will take about {minutes} minutes. Reply if you need another time.
Reminder: our {mtype} is on {date}. Please have your latest bank statements and your questions ready.
Hello {contact}, thank you for the {mtype} today. We agreed to follow up by {follow}. We will send you a short summary.
Hello {contact}, before our letter arrives: from {review_date} your monthly fee changes from {fee_now} to {new_fee}. We are happy to talk it through.
Hello {contact}, thank you for agreeing to the new monthly fee of {new_fee} from {review_date}. We will update your agreement.
Hello {contact}, we sent you our fee letter on {sent}. Can we speak this week to answer your questions?
Hello {contact}, your {service} agreement renews on {renewal}. The fee stays at {fee} per period unless you hear from us. Please tell us about any change.
Hello {contact}, thank you for confirming your {service} for another year. The updated letter is on its way.
Hello {contact}, thank you for your enquiry about {service}. Can we speak for 15 minutes this week? We will tell you what we need and what it costs.
Hello {contact}, we sent our proposal for {service} at {quote} per month. Please tell us if you would like to go through it together.
Hello {contact}, we have not heard from you for {since_touch} days. Do you still want help with {service}? A short reply is enough.
Hello {contact}, our proposal for {service} at {fee} per month ends on {expires}. Shall we keep it open or change anything?
Hello {contact}, to start your work we still need: {next_missing}. Could you send it today? {missing} items are still open.
Hello {contact}, all your onboarding checks are done. We start work on {name} now. Thank you for the quick help!
Hello {contact}, your year-end is on {next_ye}, in {days_to_ye} days. We will send the document list this week so the accounts are ready on time.
Hello {contact}, the draft accounts for {name} are ready. Please review them and reply so we can file before the deadline on {deadline}.
Hello {contact}, thank you for telling us about this. We are looking into it and will reply with a clear answer within three working days.
Hello {contact}, it has been a while since {business} left us. If your needs have changed, we would be glad to help again. Can we talk?
Hello {contact}, thank you for introducing {n_clients} clients to us. We value your trust. Your reward of {owed} is ready.
Hello {contact}, it has been {idle} days since your last introduction. Can we meet for a coffee and tell you how your clients are doing?
Hello {person}, we are updating our records for {name}. Is this still the best way to reach you, and who else should receive our reports?
Hello {contact}, we would like to hear how we are doing for {name}. Do you have 10 minutes this week for a short call?
Sample wording: adapt it to your country's law and your own practice.
Thank you for choosing {set:company}. This letter sets out the terms on which we will provide {col:engagements.service}, starting on {col:engagements.start}.

Our fee is {col:engagements.fee} per billing period, billed {col:engagements.billing}. The yearly value of this work is {col:engagements.year_value}. We review fees once a year and give {set:notice} days of written notice of any change.

Your responsibilities: provide complete and accurate records by the dates we ask, tell us promptly about changes in the business, and send us every letter from the tax authority. Late or incomplete records can delay our work and may lead to extra charges.

Our responsibilities: we will do the work with reasonable skill and care, keep your information confidential, and meet the agreed deadlines when your records arrive on time. This letter does not cover audit work or legal advice unless we agree it in writing.
This agreement renews on {col:engagements.renewal}. Either of us may end it with written notice. Please sign and return a copy to confirm that you accept these terms.
Thank you for the time you gave us. As discussed, we propose {col:proposals.service} for {col:proposals.business}.

The fee is {col:proposals.fee} per month. A one-off set-up fee of {col:proposals.setup} covers the opening of your file and the first reconciliation. The value of the first year is {col:proposals.year_value}.
This proposal was sent on {col:proposals.date} and stays open until {col:proposals.expires}. If you accept, we will send the engagement letter and the list of documents we need.
We would be glad to start with you. Please reply with any question.
Welcome letter to a new client
Welcome to {set:company}. We are glad to look after the accounts of {col:clients.name}. Your account manager is {col:clients.staff}.

In the first weeks we will complete the onboarding checks, set up your records and agree the dates for your documents. Your main package is {col:clients.package}, at {col:clients.monthly_fee} per month.
Please send us the papers on our first list as soon as you can. Your year-end is in month {col:clients.year_end}, and we will remind you well before it.
You can reach us any time. We look forward to working together.
Thank you for trusting us with {col:fee_reviews.name}. Each year we review our fees so that we can keep our service and our team strong.

From {col:fee_reviews.review_date}, your monthly fee will change from {col:fee_reviews.fee_now} to {col:fee_reviews.new_fee}, an increase of {col:fee_reviews.pct}. The main reason is: {col:fee_reviews.why}. This letter gives {set:notice} days of notice.
We are happy to explain the change and to look at how we can save you time or money in other ways. Please contact us if you would like to talk.
We confirm that our engagement with {col:lost.business} ended on {col:lost.left_on}.

We will finish and invoice all work done up to that date. On request we will return your original records and hand over to your new adviser, and we will keep our working papers for the legal retention period.
We have closed our access to your bank feeds and to the tax authority systems. Thank you for the {col:lost.months} months we worked together. You are welcome to come back at any time.
Thank you for your message of {col:complaints.date} about {col:complaints.kind}: "{col:complaints.note}"

We take this seriously. We have reviewed the file and will tell you what went wrong, what we are doing to put it right and what we will change so it does not happen again. We replied on {col:complaints.replied}.
If you are still not satisfied, please ask for a call with the partner. We value your trust.
To complete the work for {col:doc_requests.name} we need your {col:doc_requests.doc}. We asked for them on {col:doc_requests.requested} and they are due on {col:doc_requests.due}.
Please send them as a PDF or a clear photo. If something is missing, tell us and we will help you find it. Late papers can delay your filing and may lead to penalties from the tax authority.

We have been asked by {col:onboarding.contact} to act for {col:onboarding.name} from {col:onboarding.joined}. With the client's permission we ask whether there is any professional reason why we should not accept the work.
Please send, as far as you are allowed to: the latest filed accounts and tax returns, the ledgers and working papers, a list of open tax matters, and any unpaid fees. Please reply within 14 days.
Your agreement for {col:engagements.service} renews on {col:engagements.renewal}. The current fee is {col:engagements.fee} per billing period, billed {col:engagements.billing}.
If nothing changes, the agreement continues on the same terms. If your business has changed, please tell us before the renewal date so that we can update the scope and the fee.
Sample wording: adapt the reward and its conditions to your own agreement with each partner.
Thank you for introducing clients to {set:company}. So far {col:partners.n_clients} of the businesses you sent have become clients, with yearly fees of {col:partners.fee_year}.
As agreed, your reward is a share of the first-year fees. You have earned {col:partners.earned}, we have paid {col:partners.paid} and {col:partners.owed} is still to come.
We take great care of every business you trust us with. We would be glad to meet and hear how we can help your own clients.

Open Start and type your practice name and your rules in the yellow cells: target fee per hour, lowest margin, notice for a fee increase, days to finish onboarding checks and when a client needs a call.
Check the staff list and the hourly cost and charge-out rate of each person on Staff Rates. Margins and the cost of every hour come from there.
Put your price list on Fee Schedule: price, billing period and standard hours. Price per hour, margin and the discount you really give are calculated.
Add every client on Clients: contact, industry, account manager, risk level, year-end month and monthly fee. Fees, margin and health score fill in.
Record each service a client buys on Engagements with its start, agreed fee and renewal date. Yearly value and the renewal status appear by themselves.
Tick off the five checks for a new client on Onboarding Checks, and file the contacts and their roles on Contacts and Roles.
Add your monthly hours per client and person on Client Hours and the hours available on Staff Capacity to see margin, utilisation and who is overloaded.
Chase papers on Documents Requested and note every call on Meetings and Calls, with the follow-up date and whether it is done.
Plan next year's fees on Fee Reviews. The letter date follows your notice period and the extra yearly income is added up.
Track enquiries on Leads and quotes on Proposals, and list your banks, lawyers and other introducers on Referral Partners to see their reward.
Score each client on Risk Assessment and Client Health, then watch the dates on Year-end Calendar.
Log every Complaint and every client who leaves on Lost Clients with the reason and the win-back date.
Print a client card, engagement sheet or letter from the printable sheets by typing the ID in the yellow cell.
Tap a message link on any sheet to open WhatsApp with the text already written; all wording is on the Messages sheet.
Use the calculators to quote a new client, plan a fee increase, check the fee per hour and see if the team has room.
Read the Practice Dashboard and Charts every week: renewals, overdue papers, health, capacity and lost fees at a glance.
Timesheets, invoices, receivables and collections for your accounting practice
Timesheets, invoices, receivables and collections for your practice in one file
each line takes the staff rate for its service, so time shows its value at standard rates, its cost and whether it is billed, unbilled or covered by a fee
Work in progress with unbilled time ageing
hourly work not yet invoiced is added up for each client with the age of the oldest line and a bill now, bill with next invoice or nothing to bill flag
Invoices with tax, ageing and late fees
tax, total, payments, credit notes, write-offs and retainers give the balance, days overdue, status, ageing bucket and the late fee built up
what each client owes in each bucket, the oldest bucket, days since the last call and a priority from call today to no action
the value of the time at standard rates against the fees really kept after credits and write-offs, with fee per hour and margin for every client
actual hours from the timesheet against the budget, fee per hour, margin and an over-budget warning show whether the fixed fee was priced right
Staff utilisation and margin by month
hours worked and billable hours against hours available, time value, cost and average rate for each staff member and month
Promises to pay kept or missed
every collection call logs the promise and the sheet checks the payments to say if it was kept, missed or is still waiting
Payment plans that track every instalment
instalments paid and due, missed instalments, the next due date and a status of on plan, behind or completed from the matching payments
Bad debt reserve from your own rates
each ageing bucket times its rate from your settings plus an extra reserve for disputes, with the cover and risk for every client
money held for clients, drawn down by the invoices that use it, with the balance, months of fees it covers and a running-low warning

One row for each client with payment terms and the money picture: billed, received, open and overdue balance, last payment and how many days late they usually pay; it fills in from the other sheets.
Charge-out rates and cost per hour by staff and service
One row for each staff member and type of service: the rate you charge and what an hour costs you. Hours, time value and margin earned over 12 months fill in from the Timesheet.
One line for each stretch of work: who, which client and service, hours and how it is billed. Rate, value, cost and whether the time is billed, unbilled or covered by a fee come out by themselves.
Work in progress: unbilled time by client
One row for each client with hourly work not yet on an invoice: hours, value, days since the oldest line and what to do. Time covered by a fixed or monthly fee is not counted here.
Invoices with tax, payments and balance
Every invoice you issue. Tax, total, payments, credit notes, write-offs, balance, days overdue, status, ageing bucket and late fee come from the other sheets, so late payers show themselves.
Payments received and matched to invoices
One row for each payment: who paid, which invoice, how and how much. Days after the due date, on time or late, and the share of the invoice paid are worked out for you.
Credit notes given against invoices, with the reason and who approved them. Tax reversed, net amount and what is still owed on the invoice come out by themselves.
One row for each client with what they owe in each ageing bucket, the oldest bucket, days since your last call and a priority for collection; it reads the Invoices and Collection Calls sheets.
Retainers and deposits held for clients
Money received in advance, drawn down by invoices that use it. Applied, balance left, months of fees it still covers and a running-low warning come out by themselves.
Every discount, small balance and bad debt you take off an invoice, with the reason and who approved it. Share of the invoice follows, and amounts over your limit are flagged.
Plans agreed with clients who cannot pay in one go: amount, deposit and instalments. Paid so far, missed instalments, next due date and status come from the Payments sheet.
Collection calls and promises to pay
A log of every call, message or visit about money owed: who, how, what was said and any promise to pay. It checks the Payments sheet and tells you whether each promise was kept or missed.
Fixed-fee jobs: budget against actual hours
Annual accounts, tax returns and set-up projects sold for a fixed fee. Actual hours come from the Timesheet; fee per hour, margin and an over-budget warning show whether the price was right.
Realisation by client: time value against fees billed
For each client, the value of the time at standard rates against the fees really billed after credits and write-offs. Realisation, fee per hour and margin show who is worth keeping at today's price.
One row for each staff member and month with the hours available. Hours worked, billable hours, utilisation, time value, cost and margin come from the Timesheet.
Expenses paid for clients and re-charged
Fees and costs you paid on a client's behalf. The amount to re-charge with your mark-up, your profit and the days waiting show which ones still need to go on an invoice.
The fees you bill again and again: monthly bookkeeping and payroll, quarterly tax returns, yearly accounts. Value a year, the next invoice date and whether it is due now or this week are worked out.
One row for each service type and month. Fees billed, invoices, hours, time value, fee per hour and realisation come out of the Invoices and Timesheet sheets, so you see which services pay.
The reserve you should hold against unpaid invoices: each ageing bucket times its rate from your settings, plus any extra amount you add for a dispute. Cover and risk show where the exposure is.
One row for each reminder or final notice you send. It shows the days overdue at the time, the late fee added and whether the invoice was paid after it, so you see which step really works.

Open Start and type your practice name and your rules in the yellow cells: payment terms, grace days, late fee rate, discount limit, write-off limit, realisation and utilisation targets and the reserve rates.
The tax rates, late fee rates and reserve rates in this workbook are your own settings. Check them with the rules where you work: this workbook helps you track money and is not tax or legal advice.
Fill Client Accounts: one row for each client with phone, who handles them and their payment terms. The money columns fill in by themselves from the other sheets.
Fill Rate Card: one row for each staff member and type of service with the hourly rate you charge and what an hour costs you. The Timesheet reads these rates.
Log time on Timesheet: date, staff member, client, service, billing basis (fixed fee, hourly or non-billable) and hours. Value, cost and whether it is billed, unbilled or covered by a fee follow.
Read Work in Progress before you invoice: hourly time not yet on an invoice is added up for each client with the age of the oldest line. Put the invoice number on the Timesheet line once you bill it.
Issue invoices on Invoices: fees, tax rate and service. Total, payments, credit notes, write-offs, balance, days overdue, status, ageing bucket and late fee update by themselves.

Enter each payment on Payments Received with the invoice number. Credit notes, write-offs and discounts go on their own sheets and reduce the balance; retainers are drawn down by the invoices that use them.

Use Receivables Ageing each week: it ranks clients by what they owe and how old it is. Log every call on Collection Calls and every reminder on Reminder Log to see which promises were kept and which step works.
Agree a payment plan on Payment Plans when a client cannot pay in one go; tag each plan payment with the plan number and the sheet tracks instalments paid, missed and the next due date.
Track fixed-fee jobs on Fixed-Fee Jobs with the budget hours, and tag the timesheet lines with the job. Fee per hour, margin and the over-budget warning show if the fee was right.
Check Realisation by Client and Staff Utilisation every month to see which clients and which people earn what your rates promise, and where hours are going unbilled.
List expenses you pay for clients on Expenses Re-charged, your repeat fees on Recurring Invoices, and read Revenue by Service and Bad Debt Reserve for the totals and the reserve you should hold.
Use the 14 calculators to build an invoice, work out a late fee, check a discount, price a job by the hour or fixed fee, test a rate rise, plan a payment plan, forecast cash and plan capacity.

Print invoices, statements, receipts and job cards from the printable sheets and letters by choosing the number in the yellow cell, and tap a message link to open WhatsApp with the text already written.
Read Billing Dashboard and Charts each week: billed against cash, overdue money, unbilled work, utilisation, realisation and the reserve at a glance.
